findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed both a sanitizer bucket and the sanitizer dispenser to reach a concentration of 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the line was ran for several minutes until air bubbles passed. Frequently monitor the concentration of chemicals used to sanitize food contact surfaces using test strips as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) Soda nozzles at the drive thru contain a significant accumulation of biofilm.
2) Soda nozzles at the self service station contain a significant accumulation of biofilm.
3) The ice scoop holder for the ice machine.
4) The lid of the soft serve machine.
CORRECTED- food contact surfaces were removed to be cleaned and sanitized at the triple sink. Discussed removing nozzles to be cleaned with a brush and sanitized daily. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris which may contaminate ready to eat foods and drinks.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the tongs above the fryer station to be stored between a tray and a shelf. CORRECTED- utensil storage was discussed with the PIC and other staff members, and tongs were laid flat on the tray. In use utensils shall be stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed duct tape above the men’s restroom hand sink and to the left of the walk in cooler. Duct tape contains adhesive that will deteriorate upon exposure to splash. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Remove duct tape and refinish areas the duct tape is covering.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Spray foam near the walk-in freezer/back door needs to be cut flush and painted to leave the surface smooth and easily cleanable.
2) There are broken tiles on either side of the mop sink.
Repair physical facilities to eliminate gaps and create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: A food employee was observed wearing gloves to deliver food to customers in the dining room, return to the kitchen, and return to food preparation without washing hands or changing gloves. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will review when to wash hands with employees. Ensure employees wash hands upon entering the kitchen prior to engaging in food preparation without washing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: A food employee was observed rinsing a milkshake cup in the front counter handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will review handsink use with employees. Ensure handsinks are ONLY used for handwashing, no other purpose.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Sticky fly strips were observed installed in several locations around the 3 compartment sink and clean dish storage. CORRECTED- PIC removed the fly strips and relocated them to use in the dry storage area. Fly strips may be put up overnight when no food is open in the kitchen.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Both the 3 compartment sink and the cookline handsink have leaks from the faucets. Repair sinks to eliminate the leaks.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) Spray foam near the mop sink and walk-in freezer/back door needs to be cut flush and painted to leave the surface smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Broken floor tiles in front of the fryer need to be replaced.
3) Holes in the wall behind the 3 compartment sink need to be filled.
Repair physical facilities to eliminate gaps and create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Current food handler certificates were not available for either of the two non-CFM employees present during this inspection (one is on file, but expired). Long John Silver’s is on the list of Illinois-approved food handler certificates, but PIC was unaware of this internal training and was unsure if staff have completed the course. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire, whether internally through Long John Silver’s or through another approved provider. 
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee wash hands then turn the faucet off without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- Discussed proper handwashing procedure with the employee and PIC. Ensure a barrier is used to turn the faucet off and prevent recontamination of hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Food debris was observed on the blade of the can opener. CORRECTED- PIC removed the can opener to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Clean the can opener after each use.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
No ambient air thermometer was present in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC provided a thermometer and placed it near the entrance to the walk-in cooler. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers in them.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Soil accumulation observed on the wall behind the 3 compartment sink (around the wall-mounted detergent/sanitizer dispenser). Clean often enough to prevent accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
One food handler certificate was available on file. Long John Silver’s is on the list of Illinois-approved food handler certificates, but PIC was unaware of this internal training and unsure if staff have completed the course. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire, whether internally through Long John Silver’s, or through another approved provider.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT: The ceiling is leaking along the front service counter, near the cash register, cold well, single-service storage, and fryers. Repair roof/ceiling to prevent leaks. Roofing was reported to be repaired after the previous visit. The facility is closed until the roof is repaired. Contact SCDPH for reinspection when the roof has been fixed for approval to reopen.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]
